problems: Repaired the three blocking fixes: thessaly (1332 loss split: north and east to byzantine-empire, west to despotate-of-epirus, mirroring despotate-of-epirus /ledger/40), duchy-of-the-archipelago (Tinos and Mykonos discs added to every Cyclades spec), principality-of-theodoro (Cembalo subtracted from the 1423 strip, February 1433 gain added, keyframe split 1423-1432 / 1433 / 1434-1475). All three validate with --resolve (0 errors, 0 warnings). Also applied unrequested thin-item results: Licario loss moved 1277 to 1278 (confidence 1), 1295 and Mangup/Gothia notes; extra pages (Nikephoros I, John II Doukas, Marco II Sanudo, Mangup, Gothia) exceed the 1-2 page budgets and are in each dossier's sources.

Routed to the owner of byzantine-empire (eu-05, another part): /ledger/172 (1333 gain of all 'Thessaly' from thessaly) must be split like thessaly's /ledger/5-6 (Larissa 50 km disc in 1332/3; the western part only after John II Orsini's death, about 1335/6, matching despotate-of-epirus /ledger/41). Its missing mirror of Licario's Cycladic gains and their 1310 loss should use 1278 for the duchy's islands, not 1277.

Gazetteer: the 'Cyclades' region resolves to six cells and contains no cell at Tinos or Mykonos, so on today's grid the new Tinos and Mykonos discs remove no extra cell; the region also omits Syros, Kea, Paros, Sifnos which have land cells. The duchy is drawn too thin until the region is rebuilt.

Grid artefact in principality-of-theodoro: Balaklava has no land cell; the 15 km Cembalo disc of the 1433/1434 gain, loss and contest events and of /wars/1 resolves to the Inkerman and Mangup cells, i.e. Theodoro's own core, so a renderer that applies the 1434 loss as a cell removal would remove Mangup. The keyframes avoid this (Cembalo is subtracted from the coastal discs only). Treat those events as notes-only or give Cembalo a land cell.

thessaly: the Larissa 50 km disc is a reading, not a page boundary; the Medieval Thessaly page says the Byzantines took the 'northern and western part' while the Stephen Gabrielopoulos page says 'northern and eastern' (Ferjancic: 'eastern and central'); the dossier follows the latter, as despotate-of-epirus does. The reviewer's other thin and open points remain in the notes file.
